expl: Hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs) are a group of synthetic gases primarily used for cooling and refrigeration. HFCs are entirely man-made. They are primarily produced for use in refrigeration, air-conditioning, insulating foams and aerosol propellants, with minor uses as solvents and for fire protection. stem: Ozone layer of upper atmosphere is being destroyed by which of the following?
expl: When chlorine and bromine atoms make contact with ozone in the stratosphere, they destroy ozone molecules. One chlorine atom of chlorofluorocarbon can destroy over 100,000 ozone molecules before it is removed from the stratosphere. Ozone can be destroyed more quickly than it is naturally created.

stem: Which of the following is used in fire alarm?
expl: The photocell is used in fire alarm. A photocell is a technological application of the photoelectric effect. A photocell is a resistor that changes resistance depending on the amount of light incident on it. It operates on semiconductor photoconductivity - the energy of light photons hitting the semiconductor frees electron to flow, decreasing the resistance. Photocell fire alarm device projects a continuous, focused beam of light onto a mirror. If nothing interferes with the beam en route and back, the sensor perceives no obstruction. But when a small amount of smoke enters the chamber, the light is refracted slightly, causing an alarm to sound.

expl: A soda-acid fire extinguisher contains a solution of sodium bicarbonate (baking soda) and Sulfuric acid, which, when mixed, produce carbon dioxide gas that helps extinguish fires by displacing oxygen. Sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO) is the 'soda' part of the extinguisher, while Sulfuric acid (HSO) is the 'acid' part, and it's a diluted solution of Sulfuric acid. When the Sulfuric acid comes into contact with the sodium bicarbonate solution, a chemical reaction occurs, producing carbon dioxide (CO), water (HO), and sodium sulphate (NaSO). 2 4 The carbon dioxide gas produced by the reaction displaces oxygen, which is needed for combustion, thus smothering the fire.

stem: Dichloro-diphenyl-trichloroethane (DDT) is a :

Some countries outside the United States still use DDT to control of mosquitoes that spread malaria. DDT and its related chemicals persist for a long time in the environment and in animal tissues.

stem:
With reference to ‘Direct Air Capture’, an emerging technology, which of the following statements is/are correct?
I. It can be used as a way of carbon sequestration.
II. It can be a valuable approach for plastic production and in food processing.
III. In aviation, it can be a source of carbon for combining with hydrogen to create synthetic low-carbon fuel.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.

options.label: d
options.text: None of the above statements is correct

expl: ‘Direct Air Capture (DAC)’ is an emerging technology that removes CO directly from ambient air. The U.S. Department of Energy describes DAC as a means of “separating CO from ambient air and then either storing it permanently underground or converting it into products.” Direct Air Capture (DAC) technologies remove CO from ambient air using liquid solvents or solid sorbents, which is then stored permanently underground (sequestration) or utilized to create products. The captured CO can be used directly or indirectly in fuels, plastics or even building materials after processing and possible transportation. Major applications include synthetic fuel production, construction materials (concrete), and food/beverage industries. In some cases – jet fuel, for example – products produced with captured CO could still be a favourable substitute for more emissions-intensive fossil fuels. Thus, All three statements are consistent with the current scientific and industrial uses of DAC.

stem: Which one among the following is called philosopher's wool?
expl: The compound Zinc Oxide (ZnO) is called philosopher’s wool. Alchemists, as part of their rituals, would burn zinc in air and collect the residue, which formed into white woolly tufts. They called it lana philosophica in Latin, meaning philosopher's wool. Zinc oxide has many uses such as white pigment in paints, component in zinc ointment for treating skin diseases, material in sun screens and sun lotions, in rubber manufacture and in photocopying products.

expl: The scientists have discovered the heaviest antimatter ever observed in 2011 at Brookhaven National Laboratory of U.S.A. stem: In the context of which of the following do some scientists suggest the use of cirrus cloud thinning technique and the injection of sulphate aerosol into stratosphere?

options.text: Creating the artificial rains in some regions

options.label: b
options.text: Reducing the frequency and intensity of tropical cyclones

options.label: c
options.text: Reducing the adverse effects of solar wind on the Earth

expl: For reducing the global warming geo-engineering solutions have often been suggested by the scientists. Injection of sulphate aerosols, very fine solid particles, into the stratosphere is one of the most widely discussed ideas. Sulphate aerosol particles are very good reflectors of sunlight, and it has been shown, through various climate models, that even if 1% of current incident solar radiation is reflected back in space, a very significant amount of temperature rise on Earth can be offset. Another way of instantly cooling the planet is the use of cirrus cloud thinning technique. These clouds are composed mainly of ice crystals and they have greenhouse property. They let the solar radiation pass through and reach the surface, but trap the higher wavelength infrared radiation emitted from the Earth, thereby contributing to the heating. If these clouds are reduced by some engineering interventions, it would allow the IR radiation from the Earth, too, to pass through to space, thus allowing some of the heat to dissipate and hence cool the planet.

expl: Water vapour is a variable gas in the atmosphere, the amount of which decreases with altitude. In the warm and wet tropics, it may account for about four percent of the air by volume, while in the dry and cold areas of desert and polar regions, it may be less than one percent of the air. Water vapour also decreases from the equator towards the poles. It also absorbs parts of the insolation from the sun and preserves the Earth’s radiated heat. It thus, acts like a blanket allowing the Earth neither to become too cold nor too hot. Water vapour also contributes to the stability and instability in the air. Hence, statement 1 is correct, while statement 2 is incorrect.

stem:
The World Bank warned that India could become one of the first places where wet-bulb temperatures routinely exceed 35°C. Which of the following statements best reflect(s) the implication of the above-said report?
I. Peninsular India will most likely suffer from flooding, tropical cyclones and droughts.
II. The survival of animals including humans will be affected as shedding of their body heat through perspiration becomes difficult.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
expl: Wet-bulb temperature is an index that combines both air temperature and humidity to indicate the actual heat stress on the human body. It assesses the effect on the body more accurately than air temperature alone. In global studies, a wet-bulb temperature of 35°C is considered the upper tolerable limit for human life; at this level, sweat cannot evaporate to cool the body, so the body cannot dissipate its excess heat. A recent World Bank report (November, 2022) has estimated that India could be among the first places where, in the future, wet-bulb temperature may exceed the 35°C 'survivability threshold', and millions of people could face the risk of deadly heat waves. As per the report, India will witness rising temperatures and heat stress due to climate change and wet-bulb temperatures are projected to approach the 35°C threshold under IPCC's future climate scenario (RCP8.5) by the end of the 21st century over the Ganges River Valley, North-Eastern India, eastern coast of India, and Chota Nagpur Plateau. The World Bank report warning mentioned here mainly focuses on wet-bulb temperature rising above 35°C, which is directly related to the physical survival of humans and other organisms– not specifically to floods, cyclones, or droughts in peninsular India. Therefore, Statement I cannot be considered correct. Statement II directly reflects the survival-related impact on humans and other living beings due to wet-bulb temperature crossing 35°C. Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

expl: Magnetite is an oxide formed by iron ions of valences 2+ and 3+. Biologically formed nanoparticles of the strongly magnetic mineral, magnetite, were first detected in the human brain over 25 years ago. These brain magnetites display compelling similarity with the magnetite nanospheres formed by combustion, which are ubiquitous and prolific in urban, airborne pariculate matter (PM). Magnetite can have potentially large impacts on the brain due to its unique combination of redox activity, surface charge, and strongly magnetic behaviour. Magnetite could be toxic to the brain, generating harmful reactive oxygen species that have been linked to Alzheimer's disease. In addition to occupational settings (including, for example, exposure to printer toner powders), higher concentrations of magnetite pollution nanoparticles are likely to arise from open fires and vehicles (tailpipe and brake wear) and/or industrial (power plants) PM sources. There are no clear evidence of generation of magnetic particles from microwave stoves within homes or from telephone lines. Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

expl: Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) is executing a nation-wide programme of ambient air quality monitoring known as National Air Quality Monitoring Programme (NAMP). The network as on November, 2024 consists of 966 operating stations covering 419 cities/towns. The objectives of the N.A.M.P. are to determine status and trends of ambient air quality; to ascertain whether the prescribed ambient air quality standards are violated; to Identify Non-attainment Cities; to obtain the knowledge and understanding necessary for developing preventive and corrective measures and to understand the natural cleansing process undergoing in the environment through pollution dilution, dispersion, wind based movement, dry deposition, precipitation and chemical transformation of pollutants generated. Under N.A.M.P., earlier four air pollutants viz., Sulfur Dioxide (SO ), Oxides of Nitrogen (as NO ), Respirable Suspended Particulate Matter (RSPM/PM ) and Fine Particulate Matter (PM ) were identified for regular monitoring at all the 2.5 locations. At Present, only first three among these have been regularly monitored at all the locations, while PM is monitored at 611 stations in 277 cities. The monitoring of meteorological parameters such as wind speed and wind direction, relative humidity (RH) and temperature were also integrated with the monitoring of air quality.

stem: Steam methane reforming technique is used to obtain:
expl: Steam methane reforming (SMR) is a widely used industrial process for producing hydrogen and carbon monoxide (syngas) by reacting methane (natural gas) with steam at high temperatures (700 – 1000°C) in the presence of a catalyst, typically nickel-based. The main purpose of this technology is often hydrogen production, although syngas has multiple other uses such as production of ammonia or methanol. The main chemical reaction is : CH + HO → CO + 3H. To further increase hydrogen production, the carbon monoxide produced in the SMR reaction can be reacted with steam in a "water-gas shift reaction" : CO + HO → CO + H. SMR is a primary method for hydrogen production, used in various industries, including fuel cells, ammonia synthesis, and the production of other chemicals. Hydrogen produced by steam reforming is termed as 'grey' hydrogen when the waste carbon dioxide is released to the atmosphere and 'blue' hydrogen when the carbon dioxide is (mostly) captured and stored geologically. Hence, option (b) is the correct answer. • Made from Coal • Made from CH • CO is emitted into • CO is emitted into

expl: Green Hydrogen, produces using renewable energy, has the potential to play a key role in low-carbon and self-reliant economic pathways. It can directly replace fossil fuel derived feedstocks in petroleum refining, fertilizer production, steel manufacturing etc. Hydrogen fuelled long-haul automobiles and marine vessels can enable decarbonisation of the mobility sector. In the recent years, pilot projects have been undertaken in India for production of Green Hydrogen through electrolysis of water using renewable electricity, and from biomass through thermochemical and biochemical routes. The 'National Green Hydrogen Mission' aims to provide a comprehensive action plan for establishing a Green Hydrogen ecosystem and catalysing a systemic response to the opportunities and challenges of this sunrise sector. The Mission aims to develop and scale up Green Hydrogen production technology and make it affordable and widely accessible. Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

stem: Smog is essentially caused by the atmospheric presence of
expl: Smog is a type of intense air pollution. The word 'smog' is a contraction of the words smoke and fog to refer the smoky fog. It is a kind of visible air pollution and is composed of nitrogen oxides, Sulfur oxides, ozone, smoke and other particulates. Man-made smog is derived from coal combustion emissions, vehicular emissions, industrial emissions, forest and agricultural fires and photochemical reactions of these emissions.

stem: Photochemical smog always contains :
expl: Photochemical smog is a brownish-gray haze caused by the action of solar ultraviolet radiation on atmosphere polluted with hydrocarbons and oxides of nitrogen. It contains anthropogenic air pollutants, mainly ozone, nitric acid, and organic compounds, which are trapped near the ground by temperature inversion. Ozone is the principal component of air pollution of this kind. Photochemical smog appears to be initiated by nitrogen oxides that are emitted into the air as pollutants mainly from internal combustion engines. Absorbing the visible or ultraviolet energy of sunlight, it forms nitric oxide (NO) to free atoms of oxygen (O), which then combine with molecular oxygen (O) to form ozone (O). In the presence of hydrocarbons (other than methane), 3 certain other organic compounds, and sunlight, various chemical reactions take place to form photochemical smog – a mixture of ozone, nitric acid, aldehydes, peroxyacyl nitrates (PANs) and other secondary pollutants.

expl: Eutrophication is excessive richness of nutrients in a lake or other body of water, frequently due to run-off from the land, which causes a dense growth of plant life. This induces excessive growth of algae and this process depletes dissolved oxygen of the water. Eutrophication is often induced by the discharge of nitrate or phosphate-containing detergents, fertilizers, or sewage into an aquatic system.

Such man-made eutrophication is caused by the excessive discharge of nutrients, especially phosphorous (P) in the form of phosphate, nitrogen (N) in the form of nitrate, and silicate.

stem: Biological Oxygen Demand (BOD) is a standard criterion for –

options.label: b
options.text: Computing oxygen levels in forest ecosystems

options.label: d
options.text: Assessing oxygen levels in high altitude regions

expl: Biological Oxygen Demand (BOD) is a standard criterion for pollution assay in aquatic ecosystems. BOD is the amount of oxygen consumed by bacteria and other microorganisms while they decompose organic matter under aerobic conditions. Bacteria and other microorganisms consume dissolved oxygen in water bodies to decompose organic matter or waste, which reduces the amount of dissolved oxygen in water. The decrease in the amount of dissolved oxygen means increase in its demand. Higher BOD indicates more oxygen is required, signifying lower or infected water quality. Therefore, the demand for oxygen is directly related to the amount of increasing waste. Where there is high BOD, there will be low dissolved oxygen.

The outflow of polluted water is mainly done in rivers, lake, sea, etc.

stem: 'Membrane Bioreactors' are often discussed in the context of:
expl: A Membrane Bioreactor (MBR) is a chemical equipment that combines a membrane separation process with a conventional wastewater treatment process. MBRs are commonly used in municipal and industrial wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs). In the MBR process, membranes act as a solid-liquid separation device, keeping the biomass within the bioreactor before discharging the treated effluent to the nature. Basically, they take the place of bulky clarifiers used in the conventional activated sludge (CAS) process.

stem:

Statement II : Activated carbon exhibits a large surface area and a strong potential for adsorbing heavy metals.
Statement III : Activated carbon can be easily synthesized from environmental wastes with high carbon content.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?

options.label: a
options.text: B oth Statement II and Statement III are correct and both of them explain Statement I.

options.label: b
options.text: Both Statement II and Statement III are correct but only one of them explains Statement I.

options.label: c
options.text: O nly one of the Statements II and III is correct and that explains Statement I.

options.label: d
options.text: Neither Statement II nor Statement III is correct.

expl: Statement I says that activated carbon is a 'good and attractive means' for removing pollutants from effluent streams and for the remediation of polluted water generated by various industries. Activated carbon is a highly effective, porous adsorbent for removing heavy metals (such as lead, cadmium, nickel, and copper) from wastewater and drinking water due to its large surface area and oxygen-containing functional groups. It captures ions via physical adsorption and surface complexation, offering high, cost-effective removal capacities. Thus, Statement II is correct, and it explains why activated carbon is highly effective in removing pollutants (especially heavy metals and other dissolved impurities). Statement III is also correct, stating that activated carbon can be easily synthesized from carbon-rich environmental wastes. Hence, Statement II and Statement III are both correct, and together they explain–through two different aspects– the 'good and attractive means' described in Statement I.

stem: In the context of which one of the following are the terms ‘pyrolysis and plasma gasification’ mentioned?
expl: Like incineration, pyrolysis and plasma gasification technologies are thermal processes that use high temperatures to break down waste. The main difference is that they use nil or less oxygen than traditional mass-burn incineration. Plasma gasification system facilitates safe disposal of all type of organic wastes. The inorganic waste materials like glass, metals, plastics can also be minimized to slag. In plasma pyrolysis the most likely compounds which are produced include carbonaceous matter, methane, carbon monoxide, hydrogen, carbon dioxide and water molecules. The product gases recovered has calorific and commercial values. These gases can be used as a heat source or as fuel. NITI Ayog in his three-year Action Agenda (2017-2020), also assessed the benefit-cost ratio of thermal pyrolysis and plasma gasification as waste-to-energy technologies.

Mercury is a toxic substance that severely contaminates land, water, air and the food chain. Which among the following is/are source(s) of mercury pollution?
I. Pesticides
II. Dental amalgam fillings
III. Fluorescent lamp
IV. Coal-based thermal power plants

options.label: d
options.text: I, II, III and IV all

expl: Pesticides, Dental amalgam fillings, fluorescent lamp and coal-based thermal power plants, all of these are sources of mercury pollution.
